prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1429; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver, who is named on the policy. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reported a knee injury at the scene.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the collision happened as described. The other driver's statement matches the account given to us.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene were reviewed. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact, and nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage start date.

Entry 4: Vehicle history shows no earlier damage on record. The claimant's medical records show no prior injury to the same knee.

Entry 5: The claimant later added a few small details about the sequence of events, but the core account stayed the same across each conversation. Reported injury appears consistent with the kind and force of the crash.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Treatment tapered off as the claimant's knee improved and the provider noted steady recovery.

Entry 7: Based on the consistent accounts, scene photos, and medical timeline, the claim is proceeding through standard evaluation with no open questions on liability or causation.
